text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White Black Friday sales have brought the Echo Dot to under $30, and that is how I am now buying my second one.

So yes, often times you do need to formulate your requests in a certain way (for instance, try asking Alexa how much time it will take to go to work... I gave up on this...) and enunciate them more clearly if you missed, but in general, this technology is just amazing.
Sometimes I even ask Alexa for information I don't need, just for fun.

I like that they named it Alexa. That's so much better than "Okay Google." It feels like a real person. Who in hell at Google thought it's a good idea to force users to use their company name, and thus remind them that their huge creepy analytics private data gathering network is behind it?

Possible improvements:
* Bring back the matte finish from 1st gen. I shouldn't have to pay more to not have it shiny...
* Listen to the word "stop" when the alarm is ringing. Currently you need to wait until it's not ringing and then say "Alexa, stop."
* Add confirmation and modification prompts to "Add a new event to the calendar." Currently if she misunderstood one word, you have to start all over again.
* Alexa bluntly tells you that she cannot tell you about the events in your calendar on a specific date... C'mon guys...
* Implement the word "Repeat": sometimes you didn't hear or didn't catch the information you were looking for, and currently you have to formulate your request again
* Only gives info about the last Amazon order. She can retrieve more order but you have to be very specific about what they contain.
* I wish Alexa could Google more stuff.
* Choose your own wake up word

I never use Siri on my iPhone, but for some reason it feels very natural to use Alexa, maybe because the device is more "fixed" whereas my phone could be in a backpack, in the other room...

The Killer App is MUSIC. We have an Echo Dot in the bedroom, and my wife just loves to ask Alexa for tunes. We have it linked to Spotify.

Also, I am a software engineer, and I have added some custom features through my own skills. I wish somebody came up with something simple to add your own skills, because this is really useful. For instance, the bus comes in front of my house at the most random times, so I developed a skill that tells me in how many minutes the next buses will come. So much faster than having to check a website on my phone!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

There are 3 relatively easy and inexpensive ways to make it perform as good or better than new. First is to add more memory, though older 32-bit computers may be limited in how much memory you can add. Second do some housecleaning by removing unused software and reinstalling the operating system. Third is to install a solid-state drive like this one. It installs just like an old-fashioned hard drive, but runs tremendously faster. Install your operating system and frequently used files on here and your computer will feel like better than new, especially when starting up and when launching large application programs. This drive has been very reliable for me so far. In the long run, I expect it to be more reliable than a traditional hard drive (which is often the most fragile part of a computer).

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] I have always loved the Keyboard version (and still do), but unfortunately without the benefit of backlighting and the poor selection of cases with adequate lighting (I've ordered and returned several), I started to use it less and less - and used my Iphone App almost exclusively. But I really wanted to use a Kindle which was designed primarily for reading books as opposed to the small screen of a Smart phone. And I'm not about to go lugging around an Ipad day after day.

Last year I purchased a Kindle Touch but was extremely unhappy with the instability of the touch screen and other issues with that model. So I bought the aforementioned Keyboard and made do with it. I should add that I have owned five Kindles since their launch in 2007. When the Paperwhite was announced, I immediately got one for my husband while I waited for a 3g model for myself.

Initially I was a little disappointed with the Paperwhite because of my own lack of patience and constant comparing it to my other devices. I had to get use to swiping the screen to wake it up, understand the basic settings operations, and generally become comfortable with this model. I have to admit that I had contacted Amazon about sending it back within a couple of days of receiving it, but for some reason (maybe maturity?), I decided to keep it for another few days just to play with it a bit more.

I am so glad that I did. My only complaint is that I wish Amazon would have included some kind of cheat sheet to get users started. It would have gone a long way to prevent my initial meltdown. If my husband hadn't had his own Paperwhite for a month and shown me all of the basics, I can assure you that this model would be back in the hands of Amazon employees right now. They don't need to include some overwhelming instruction manual. Just one piece of paper with some simple "how to" notes would be perfect - I'd even be willing to draft something up for them!

Now that I've settled down with my Paperwhite, and have begun to take advantage of the outstanding benefits that it offers (i.e. instant dictionary, reading in the dark, lightweight and gorgeous, etc.) I would not part with it for anything. And my Keyboard is about to become a special gift to a friend who has always wanted a Kindle.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System This is the best record cleaning I tried so far. I is very effective in removing dust (and associated static noise) from records that are in reasonably good shape. Of course, it cannot repair records which have been damaged due to being played while dirty. If you acquire a used record in dirty condition, it is probably a good idea to wash it with distilled water first before using the discwasher on it.

I noticed that there are several one-star reviews complaining about the direction of fibers on the cleaning pad that comes with this system. Yes, the cords of the corduroy-like microfiber material does run along the edge of the brush, but this is actually how it should be to provide even coverage across all the grooves. The cords of any fabric is much too thick to fit into the actual grooves on the record. If the cords were to run along the direction of the the grooves, some grooves would be cleaned and some wouldn't. Having the cords being perpendicular to the grooves on the record ensures that all grooves get cleaned evenly. After all, it is the microfibers, not the cords of the fabric, doing the cleaning.

Another advantage of cords running perpendicular to the grooves of the record is that, as you slowly rotate the brush on its axis (as shown in the provided directions), dust that has been collected gets trapped between the cords that are being lifted off the record as the next (clean) cord of the fabric starts making contact with the record surface.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System

Canon EF 70-200mm f/4 L is USM Lens for Canon Digital SLR Cameras I upgraded to this lens from the non-IS version of the 70-200mm as I was having problems getting sharp shots not affected by hand shake. The lens is rather long and heavy and the image stabilization comes in quite handy, especially with shots under low light conditions when you don't want to raise the ISO too high to compensate. The IS can generally get you 2 stops more light than what you might ordinarily expect before experiencing hand shake blur.

Images from this lens are very nice - sharp and good color, good bokeh at the wider apertures so you get nice separation between subject and background. I took this lens to the zoo once and got lots of good shots with it, I've been very pleased with its performance.

I use this lens on a full-frame camera, so keep in mind that if you are buying this for a camera with a cropped sensor, the actual focal range is more like a 110-320mm.

Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras The Canon 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 lens with Image Stabilization is a very capable, and more importantly, affordable lens,and is perfect for times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. While you get the benefits of a slight wide to telephoto range in one handy package, you do lose in light stops as you move through the focal range (the maximum aperture stops down as you move toward the telephoto end of the range). This is where the image stabilization comes in very handy, and allows you to keep hand shake at bay even when you have to compromise on shutter speed to get the correct exposure.

I've had no complaints about the optical quality, I think you'll be pleased with the shots you get from it - the lens may be cheap but don't confuse that with what the quality of image this lens can provide. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @45-215mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.
text_fidelity_b: Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras 48 LED unit - (since several items are listed under one product ID)
Positives:
- It is what it looks like, does what it claims to do, and basically works
- cheap
- comes with an AC adapter!! Wow. You can pay a lot for a light that doesn't

Negatives: I'm using this for Macro work (I'm new to macro) so that's the perspective I'm coming from
- Not Bright Enough! It's just not all that bright. Not enough to light a subject by itself for macro purposes. I doubt it's adequate for more than a highlight for portraiture. This is why 2 stars. If a light doesn't light - it's not a light.

Really that's it. This is not a knock to the light (and not why I gave it a low rating), but if you are planning on using it for macro, buy a flash instead. A flash will not only have higher output, but will help freeze the camera shake (a big macro problem). Also, I thought the full time light would be better for live insects (you can see what you're doing!), but it's the opposite. You need the flash to freeze action. Not a criticism (this light does not advertise itself as a flash), but something to know.

UPDATE: I used it a couple more times. I am finding it more useful than initially when very close in. I would still strongly recommend a flash for this unless you have a compelling reason for continuous illumination (e.g you're waiting for a bug to crawl into frame and it's too dark to see otherwise. Though the lights would probably scare the bug). If you have a pretty solid tripod setup, this can work for longer exposure macro. Not great though. Upped to 3 stars.

text_fidelity_a: Canon PowerShot SX50 HS 12MP Digital Camera with 2.8-Inch LCD (Black) - International Version (No Warranty) I  loved this little camera. Great features and photos. In first couple weeks had a problem--the screen regularly froze and camera turned off. Fortunately Amazon as always was great and I returned for another. After 6 months the zoom started wobbling. Sent it to Canon for repair. Got an email saying they didn't work on that part, I'd get a new or refurbished. I called to say i did not want a refurbished camera given that i'd already had problems with two of this model.  Too bad they said, you're getting refurbished.  I asked to talk to customer relations. Got a lady who told me it was in the warranty they could give me refurbished and furthermore they had no new ones to give--this is the CAnon facility mind you.  I called back to try to talk to another rep--was told they couldln't transfer me. Then, when i said i was recording it, and told him i had been transferred last time, suddenly he now could transfer me. Back to initial rep who refused to let me talk to anyone else and refused to budge on sending a new camera, even though it was an option in the email. I wrote letters and emails to management. Got a response, said they'd send me a new camera after i said i had the whole thing on recording and was thinking of posting to youtube. but they wouldn't pay for me to ship the old one back.  Anyway this story goes on and on, including me mailing the camera back and being told it actually WAS a new one and they were shipping the same camera back to me.  Was a nightmare. I don't know if any of the other companies are better, but i've been a solid Canon customer for 20 years--as i told them--and I won't be anymore.  They need to take lessons from Amazon on customer service.  Hope this camera lasts awhile as I know now it won't get serviced properly without it being more trouble than it's worth.

text_fidelity_a:
AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+ FD4100WMGUSBX My old computer was exactly that: Old! It needed some serious work. I was running an Athlon X2 6000+ and an EVGA 9800GT. It was a great system back in the day! But, time took its toll. I was kicking around the idea of getting an Intel i3, since they seem to edge out this chip, and are competitively priced (I never overclock my equipment, so it's at stock settings.) But the future upgradability seemed like it'd be very costly. Over all, this chip performs just fine. I mainly upgraded so I could play Diablo 3, and with an EVGA 550 Ti, I play it on high settings, and it looks as good as I could want it to look. My old machine did just fine with standard productivity stuff, but I wanted to play games that were more recent than WoW. I'm able to do everything I want, with no signs of a lag. If I need to upgrade, I'm banking that the next generation of this chip will see some improvements (though the improvement I'm seeing from my last CPU is leaps-and bounds!) The AM3+ socket will be around for a while. Over all, this is a great chip, and easy on the wallet.

**Update 9/6/12**
I recently purchased Guild Wars 2. The game is fairly CPU-intensive, but the FX-4100 keeps up just fine! I think I'm sitting at around 50% plus load at any given time during actual game play on all four cores. I haven't had a single hiccup or spot of lag yet!

Starcraft 2 is another CPU-heavy application, and coupled with the 550 Ti card, I'm running it on Extreme at 1400x900 resolution, and it's flawless. Again, all four cores are loaded, and quite frequently, they're over 60%. Things get a little warm (35C or so) when compared to when I run other applications. Nothing to worry about!

I have also paid quite a bit of attention to how it runs with Diablo 3. It only uses 2 cores at about 50% load at any given time. That game is more GPU-intensive. I am still very happy with my purchase!
text_fidelity_b: AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+  FD4100WMGUSBX

Tile Essentials (2020) 4-pack (1 Mate, 1 Slim, 2 Stickers) - Discontinued by Manufacturer So I bought this little bundle having lost my wallet 3 times in 2 weeks.... one of the times in another state the night before my return flight! (found it thank God).

Anyway, it's super easy to use the app and was super easy to set up these 4 little items. I used the card for my purse, the tile with the key chain hole for my car key fob and the 2 little button tiles for 2 of my TV remotes.

The point of this review is: you should know that you can buy just 1 of these things and finding your phone is an added free feature! Score! I thought I'd have to attach one of those buttons to the back of my phone, but nope! So all you do is double tap the Tile logo on any tile and it will locate my phone anywhere within bluetooth range. This is so totally awesome. I don't have to log into a computer to find my phone and I don't have to stress out looking for it when my partner's not home to ring my phone from her phone. All you have to do is double tap ANY Tile you own in bluetooth range and it'll ring your phone. How great is that???!! Can't find my phone? Grab any remote and double tap the logo - BAM! Can't find my phone? Grab my purse and double tap the logo on the card Tile - BAM! Really an A+ feature that Tile should really be clearer about when advertising their products..... like first thing.

My review doesn't include how you find things when you're out of bluetooth range..... but I think there's an alert for your phone when you're about to leave your wallet somewhere, etc., or about to exit bluetooth range.... pretty sure that's how it works. Anyway, just finding my phone and things around the house will save me how many search minutes (hours) a year??? And garners a 5 star rating on that alone.

Anyway, we'll see in time.

text_fidelity_a:

As a few others I have experienced the picture going black on the set after a few hours of operation followed by in my case a loud snapping noise. I lowered my rating based only on this phenomenon . Amazon as always stood by the sale and made everything more than right . IF it had not been for the going to black concern , my rating would have been five stars .Contacting Vizio resulted in being asked to perform a bunch of resets and chanting magic incantations ( joke ) . That was considered when raring the product too. When not going black , the picture is amazing ! Sporting events in particular pop off the screen and the detail seen is incredible. The black range is as crisp as I have ever seen on any set. Setup is very easy and uncomplicated. The remote includes a key pad on the back to make entering information and searching easier. Again , would be a five if not for the picture going black issue.

Con: The speakers are tiny and are facing the rear . Not sure why they choose to go the cheap route and skimp on the sound. By no stretch am I an audiophile but one does notice the lack of depth to the sound and the volume level needs to be up to hear dialog clearly. A sound bar is almost a requirement and I did see that some retailers are packaging one with their Vizio TV'S to,address this concern.
The remote has a quick access buttons for Amazon , Netflix and of all things IHeart Radio. They must have got a kick back from I Heart . The quick connect feature loose a plus for choosing I Heart. Hulu or the like would have been a better choice .

I would not be afraid to buy this set. I would strongly suggest that the purchase be supported by a vendor you trust and will support the sale after the fact. Some of these are through a third party and directly through Amazon . I always select the direct Amazon route because of the support after the sale. I needed it in this instance and as always was not disappointed by Amazon customer service.

I've recommended Fitbit to friends and family over and over and will continue to do so. I love that it syncs with MyFitnessPal and use that to track my food as well as my activity and recommend the same to others.

If you're looking for a really great activity tracker at a really great price, go for the Fitbit Flex.

NZXT H200i - Mini-ITX PC Gaming Case - RGB Lighting and Fan Control - CAM-Powered Smart Device - Enhanced Cable Management System – Water-Cooling Ready - Black - 2018 Model The NZXT h200i is a stunning case. The simple design beguiles the thoughtfulness that went into making this case so easy to work with. The layout is amazing, everything fits just right (for the most part) and once completed, helps your build look like it's from the future thanks to the help of the built-in RGB strip at the top of the front window. In terms of design, I could not be any happier.

The included case fans do their job and are whisper quiet most of the time. The smart hub comes pre-connected, saving the headache of trying to figure out how to hook it all up using the barebones instructions that come with the case. Overall, this case is a dream.

However, there is one glaring issue which prevents me from giving this case 5-stars. The CAM software.

Were it not for the NZXT's cam software, I would recommend this case 100% to anybody looking for a sharp case which not only shows off their build but is built well and functions amazingly. Unfortunately, I rushed to purchase the case based on looks alone and did not take my time to research the complaints regarding the CAM software. Well, now that I have worked with the CAM software, I can say that all the complaints noted by other users are true. The CAM software is garbage. When or if it does eventually load, it's great. However, most of the time I have to wait 5-10 minutes just for it to authenticate - even when logging in as a guest. I cannot fathom why my RGB lighting and fan control software requires me to log in to be used.

Since the CAM software is only used to control the lighting in the case and that's the only impact it has on the case, I decided to go with 4-stars. The case itself is amazing. The CAM software is to be avoided at all costs.

Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) When my husband recently purchased a [[ASIN:B0071N6AC6 netbook]], he wasn't using his Kindle Fire nearly as much, and I inherited it. I had recently dumped my cable TV service in favor of using the Fire to watch online the few news and TV dramas that I normally had used my TiVo to record. I found that my Internet connection through a wifi router has a really hard time playing videos via the Fire. It would often lose connectivity or freeze up when my iPhone was working fine using the same connection, playing the same shows.

The Fire has a gorgeous interface, though, for reading eBooks compared to my Kindle Keyboard. However, I've been using a Kindle app so frequently the past few months on my iPhone, that both the Kindle Keyboard and the Kindle Fire feel too cumbersome to bother with most of the time in comparison as an eReader.

For searching the Internet, the Fire has an easier interface than the iPhone, so I use it more often for that, unless I don't have it with me--I always have my iPhone with me.

I don't use the Fire for MP3. It is just too huge compared to my tiny MP3 player.

I don't have magazine subscriptions in electronic form, so I don't use it for that, though I know I could if I wanted to.

I understand the Fire can support PDF, but I haven't used it for that yet.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

I purchased this just to use as a slave to be triggered by another flash - a Yongnuo 560-II. I figured this one looked pretty similar and cost a lot less (though it's less powerful and doesn't have zooming or an LCD screen, doesn't go into sleep mode. I didn't need those things). I would should 100 shots of the same setup with the same 2 flashes -- everything the same (this was for macro - close up work). Over and over again I'd find dark frames on the Neewer TT560 side and the Yongnuo was dead on every time.

Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons I’m not a hardcore gamer anymore, so for the past few years, I’ve been using a Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball (thumb trackball). I like trackballs for everyday use, and it’s adequate for casual World of Warcraft playing. Most of the time I just futz around leveling alts or doing 5 mans with friends.

But lately I’ve been wanting a mouse I can customize, with more options to adjust my playstyle. It’s cold in my house in the winter, so I wanted to set up mouseover macros and use more mouse buttons, because my hands are cold sitting on the keyboard. So the G502 Proteus Spectrum seemed like a good mouse to review.

I just had one problem: my computer can’t customize the mouse. Why? I have a Mac Book Air.

Now, I know the G502 says on the box that it supports Windows. There’s no mention of Mac support. But I’ve never had a problem with my Mac recognizing Logitech mice, so I figured I’d be safe. What I didn’t know is that Logitech gaming mice have separate software from the Logitech Control Center for regular Logitech mice.

After some Googling, I found the Logitech Gaming Software, which supports Mac OS X 10.8.x and up. I installed it on a Mavericks machine and a Yosemite machine. Neither computer’s Logitech Gaming Software was able to find the mouse. The G502 Proteus CORE is supported, but not the G502 Proteus SPECTRUM.

So right now, I’m unable to customize any of the extra buttons or RGB lighting or any of the other special features. It’s a really fancy basic mouse. I will continue to check for Proteus Spectrum support in the Mac Logitech Gaming Center, and update this review when I can customize things. I’m going into so much detail on the Mac side of things because I know I’m not the only Mac person who tried to use this mouse. I think there’s a workaround with Bootcamp or using a Windows computer, but I’m unable to try that.

I did use the mouse for a few weeks, to test the comfort. I’m really picky on how mice feel in my hand. I’m female and have smaller hands. I like how this mouse didn’t feel too short, and it wasn’t too heavy or wide for me to use comfortably for hours at a time. I also liked the included weights, so you can adjust the weight of the mouse. I haven’t had a mouse with an adjustable weight before, and I liked that extra level of customization.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons

These buds are snug [3 different ear sizes] and cuts out a lot of external noise, although there is a hear through to bring some of the outside awareness, but it sounds more like static. I leave it off. They are so tiny compared to my other ear buds, and I have no worries about them coming off when I am running at all. The app gives some manual adjustments , but not a lot. It stayed connected with my tablet and phone and will connect to the item nearest to me. It you take one bud out to talk to someone, the music stops, and starts again once you have the bud back into your ear.
Instructions are on the website, and as there are no protruding buttons, you need to learn And practice how to take calls, adjust volumes, connect via Bluetooth.
I love Them and a huge step up in technology, design, comfort at this price point.

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(
text_fidelity_b: Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black We blow through ear buds in our house and it seems that everyone has different ones that they like and don't like. Let's see how these measure up:

WHAT ARE THESE EAR BUDS LIKE?
These ear buds come in a nice box with a little instruction booklet. There is a little bag with three sets of gel caps in it. There are also three sets of hooks. Each of them comes in small medium and large. The hooks keep the buds in the ear but are soft so they don't hurt the ear at all.

The controls are on the right ear- the top hits about where the chin is. The connecting cord is big enough to be worn in front or back. The set comes with a cord but you have to have your own USB access to plug it into whether it be on an outlet or computer.

COMFORT
One of the most comfortable and secure earbud/headsets we have used to date- love that the hooks that help hold them in are soft so they don't hurt the ear, even after worn for a while.

PERFORMANCE
VOLUME
The headset gets the best result for us with the volume on max on the headset and halfway on the tablet that we use it with.

HIGHS/LOWS/MIDS
One of the things with this headset is that the highs are really nice and strong and so are the lows. The problem seems to be that the mids are drowned out making it feel like it is a bit out of balance. We have messed with it quite a bit and it seems to be the way it is.

SOUND PROOFING
These have excellent sound insulation capabilities. That does mean, however, that you need to be careful where you are wearing them if you need to hear what is around you or not.

BATTERY ALERT
When you first turn on the headphones, it will identify itself, tell you it is pairing and then give you an idea of how much battery life you have left- low, medium, or high.

POWER BUTTON
The power button is nice. Volume/skip functions are a challenge to get used to as compared to other Bluetooth headsets. There are sequences and timing as compared to others which seem to be simpler to use.

PAIRING
Very good pairing on all of the different devices we tested this with- several phones from Moto G3, Blu phone, Samsung Tablets and our stereo (forgot brand)

CHARGE
A charge has been lasting a good six to eight hours for us. Recharging seems to take us about three hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are comfortable headphones that are easy to use, stay in the ears well, and have good insulation from ambient noise in the room or surroundings. They have nice highs and lows but tend to drown out the mids. The controls are a bit more challenging to learn at first as compared to other Bluetooth head sets we have used.

MY RATING
FOUR AND A HALF STARS- not able to give that so I am doing four. It is more like four and a half. The sound could be a little more balanced, and the controls not quite so difficult, but this is still a great set of headphones and we like it a lot.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

text_fidelity_a:
VIVO Mobile TV Cart for 13 to 50 inch Screens up to 44 lbs, LCD LED OLED 4K Smart Flat and Curved Monitor Panels, Rolling Stand, Locking Wheels, Max VESA 200x200, Black, STAND-TV07W This Vivo Mobile TV Rolling Floor Stand is a tremendous value. It is strong steel, well finished and just right for rolling my 40" Vizio (which weighs only 17 lbs) around the patio for outdoor viewing at the optimal position and height. It looks great and functions flawlessly. It assembled easily. Though it comes with a sheetmetal wrench and a 4mm Allen, I used my own 8mm and 10mm sockets to speed assembly. And a 17mm end wrench to tighten the caster jam nuts. Sadly, one tiny nut was missing; I found a replacement from my personal metric collection of miscellaneous nuts and bolts. Pay close attention to the graphical instructions. I assembled the base upside down before realizing it was wrong. Easily remedied. Also comes with a collection of TV mounting screws, washers and spacers.

I was going to mount the TV on the wall, but being off to the side and quite high, that would very much limit viewing angles and no doubt strain necks. What I really wanted was to have the TV in front of me, wherever I might be sitting and also be able to optimize for group viewing if necessary.

This little cart is exactly what I wanted. It has 2" high quality urethane casters that roll effortlessly and silently on smooth surfaces. They aren't cheap hard plastic wheels. Each caster's threaded stem screws into a tapped hole. A jam nut on the threaded stem allows you to adjust the casters so all four are on the ground, then tighten the jam nuts to lock the adjustment. No wobble! You'll need a 17mm end wrench to tighten the nuts. Two of the casters are equipped with all-lock brakes that prevent both rolling and castering so the TV stays put if desired. When I'm done, I can simply roll the TV out of the way or into the house for safe storage.The base measures 18x20 inches. My 40" TV is 36" wide. You might think it would be top heavy or unstable, but it's not for me, especially as I have the mast set to near its lowest position.

The sturdy steel telescoping mast allows me to lower the TV so that the bottom edge of the 40" TV is 24" inches from the ground -- a few inches above coffee table height. This allows a very comfortable viewing angle when sitting in my somewhat lower patio chairs. In other words, it puts the TV at a very comfortable height to avoid neck strain.

The mount is adjustable and accommodates the 200x200mm Visa mount hole pattern on my TV. It can also handle 100x200 or smaller. Other stands have very large mounting bars. This one is small, simple and compact. Be aware its max Visa mount pattern is 200x200. You can adjust for level and tilt. It can tilt up about 15 degrees. It does not tilt down. The tilt is controlled by a knob. Be aware the TV is more or less permanently mounted onto the mast and the mast is bolted tightly to the base using five fasteners with locknuts: it does not come apart easily. If you want to disassemble this device for travel, you'll need to add thumbscrews.

I did not want extraneous things like extra shelves for a DVD player. It's clean and simple. Its price is very reasonable. With all the nuts and bolts tightened securely, there is no wobble anywhere.

Couldn't he happier. it's well engineered, strong, lightweight and portable.
text_fidelity_b: VIVO Mobile TV Cart for 13 to 50 inch Screens up to 44 lbs, LCD LED OLED 4K Smart Flat and Curved Monitor Panels, Rolling Stand, Locking Wheels, Max VESA 200x200, Black, STAND-TV07W

text_fidelity_a:
OontZ Angle 3 Bluetooth Speaker, Portable Wireless Bluetooth 5.0 Speaker, 10 Watts, Crystal Clear Stereo Sound, Rich Bass, IPX5 Water Resistant, Loud Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Black) I like the speaker and it sounds good and at loud volumes there is very little distortion. It connects very easily to both my phones and tablet. A nice feature is you can answer the phone by pushing the Bluetooth button on the speaker and it will pause the audio source. Callers on the other end say they had no trouble hearing me and it was clear without echo or static. It is splash proof only if you make sure you keep the rubber door on the charging port closed.

Now for the dislikes. The main problem I have is it sounds good connect to my Surface tablet but when connected to my Cell phones, a Lumia 950 and a 950XL it cuts out repeatedly. This does not matter if I have the speaker next to or at any distance from the phones. I can overlook the other faults of this speaker but the cell phone issue make it worthless for my primary use. Maybe I got a defective unit but I am at a lost to the reason it works very well when connected to my computer and not the phones. Because of this glitch I am returning the speaker. I do not recommend this speaker if you have Lumia phones at this time. My other gripe is the rubber on the ends of the speaker are a dust magnet which you can clearly see in the photos. There is no way to keep the speaker looking good. I have another waterproof speaker and it does not exhibit the problem of dust collection. I had high hopes for the OontZ Angle since I have been using an OontZ Curve also made by Cambridge Sound Works for over 2 years without a single problem. In my humble opinion the OontZ Curve sounds a little better than OontZ Angle but not being splash proof it does not meet my needs at this time. I have been looking for a smaller splash proof speaker to take with me while traveling and I will have to continue my search.
If this review helped you or not in you buying decision please let me know. Thanks for reading
text_fidelity_b: OontZ Angle 3 Bluetooth Speaker, Portable Wireless Bluetooth 5.0 Speaker, 10 Watts, Crystal Clear Stereo Sound, Rich Bass, IPX5 Water Resistant, Loud Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black I really like this GPS sports watch so far. Garmin makes a huge range of sports watches. This vivoactive HR is one of their lower priced GPS watches. It doesn't have the more advanced sports training features or build quality of the more expensive Garmin Fenix and Forerunner watches. However, for this price, you do get GPS and smartwatch features in addition to basic fitness tracking.

I tried the GPS mode on a 3-hour bike ride, running my dedicated bicycle computer at the same time. Distance calculations of the 2 units were less than 1 mile different, which I think is very good for small portable units like this. Current speed was always about the same, though looking at the watch to see your speed while riding is kind of difficult, especially compared to the big display on my handlebar-mounted bike computer. You can mount the watch on your bicycle handlebar, but that would of course disable the heart rate tracking feature of the watch. The wrist-based heart rate monitor is not as accurate as a chest-strap heart rate monitor, with a slower response time that is very apparent during interval training (short bursts of high-intensity effort), but you can connect an ANT+ HR monitor to this watch to improve accuracy.

GPS mode has an advertised battery life of 16 hours, which I think is really terrific for a gadget of this size. My 3 hour bike ride burned about 20% of the battery on the vivo, so 16 hours of GPS time is plausible. Garmin also advertises 8 days of battery life with the GPS turned off, but realistically, who buys a $250 GPS watch and never turns on the GPS? Still, I expect to get in at least a couple of long bike rides or several runs before having to recharge this watch. Recharging is very quick using the USB charging cradle included with the watch. Because battery life is so good, you don't need a spare charger for your office like you might need with the Apple smartwatch.

If you have a (free) Garmin account, you can upload your daily activity to the Garmin server so you can review it on their website afterwards. This is useful for tracking your fitness progress (speed, distance, etc) over time.

The smartwatch features are pretty basic (compared to dedicated smartwatches from Apple or Google), showing phone call caller-ID and copying notifications from your smartphone (via Bluetooth) and displaying them on the watch. If you like checking your notifications quickly and don't want to pull your phone out every time it beeps, getting them on your watch is great. If I'm jogging or in a business meeting or at dinner but am expecting an important message, I can just glance at the watch and quickly ignore it if it isn't important. I have my notifications for high-priority emails, SMS, and a couple of messaging apps synced with my phone. This seems to work mostly flawlessly with my Samsung smartphone. Occasionally, the notifications will stop working but restarting my phone fixes that. I don't know if that is a problem with the phone's base software or with the Garmin app that runs on my phone. The Garmin app that runs on your smartphone lets you pick which app's notifications to show on the watch. I do not know how this works with Apple phones. There are some other smartwatch apps like weather forecasts and calendar, but I'm not sure if scrolling through these on your small watch face is really easier than pulling out your phone to view the app on the larger screen there.

If you're comparing this Garmin watch to an Apple smartwatch, yes Apple has a lot more apps, but Garmin has an 8 day battery life compared to less than 1 day for Apple. Personally, battery life is more valuable to me since there are not yet any killer apps for the Apple watch. Having a dead watch because you forgot to charge it the night before is not fun. Also, the Garmin watch has a built-in GPS, while the Apple watch does not. This means you can record a bike ride or run carrying only the watch, not your phone as well.

Garmin also has basic fitness tracking features like resting heart rate, sleep tracking, intensive exercise tracking, step counting, etc. If you're active enough to want to spend money a GPS sports watch (instead of a cheap fitness band), I don't think the step counting is going to be interesting to you. I bike or run at least 10 hours every week of the year and steps have no interest to me. Resting heart rate is an indicator of your health and fitness and I'm looking forward to tracking that. Intensive exercise tracking may also be useful if you tend to slack off during your exercise. Sleep tracking is reportedly not too accurate on this watch (it can't tell if you're really sleeping or reading a book in bed), but that isn't something that greatly interests me.

On the subjective side, this chunky plastic rectangular watch does look like a fitness tracker rather than a real watch. The much better looking Garmin Fenix looks like something you could wear to the office, but this watch maybe not. At least the vivoactive has a very comfortable wristband that should fit well on a range of wrist sizes.

Again, this is one of Garmin's cheaper GPS watches. I think the features and performance are great for this price point, but if you're involved in hard core training program, you should definitely look at the features of some of Garmin's better GPS watches.

I would have given this watch 5 stars for functionality and value for the price if it was better looking, but Garmin seems to have made it intentionally ugly in try to upsell you on their better looking and more expensive Fenix and Forerunner watches.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívoactive HR GPS Smart Watch, Regular fit - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Ergonomic Wireless PC Mouse - DPI adjustable - Black I selected this mouse to be a spare for when I am on the go. Amazon-branded things are often of good quality so I was hopeful for this mouse. I came away a bit disappointed due to a couple of issues I have had with it.

This is a basic wireless mouse, suitable for surfing the web, working on documents or similar tasks. It’s not particularly good for gaming as it is not designed for such. If the goal is to have something that will allow you to casually use the computer for basic tasks, this one will serve. If you need a heavy-duty mouse for frequent use or you need a gaming mouse, spend a little more and get a more solid mouse.

One of the issues I have with mice is that I have huge hands and finding a mouse that fits my hand properly is a challenge. This is a smaller than average mouse, so it really doesn’t work for me. That’s not a big deal; it was designed for the large majority of people with smaller hands, so I can’t criticize this mouse for its size. It’s in that weird in-between size - smaller than the average desktop mouse but larger than a travel mouse.

The real issue I have seen with this mouse, though, is with the DPI setting. After idling for a little while, the mouse has a very nasty and predictable habit of resetting the DPI mode automatically. This is the only mouse I have used that has exhibited the problem. This impacts me when I am doing photo editing or using a graphics program and I need fine control. Sure, I can hit the DPI setting and get it to where I need it to be easily enough, but I should not have to do this over and over, particularly when I need the same setting all the time.

Other than the DPI setting, this mouse works exactly as expected. It is a decent mouse if you do not need predictable DPI settings. If you need a mouse that retains your settings, or if you need a larger mouse, or if you need a heavy-duty device, this is not the right choice for you. It’s fine for travel or casual use.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Ergonomic Wireless PC Mouse - DPI adjustable - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sony DCR-SX45 Handycam Camcorder (Blue) The camcorder was bought to record some interviews and later to be used for general videos. It worked very well for the interviews with excellent image quality and color balance. The audio was good but not great with the built-in microphone, something that I expected.

I have tried to use it for other general videos with a fair number of action shots of animals, planes and other moving targets. I find the screen to be difficult to see in direct sunlight, one of the main reasons I strongly prefer an optical viewfinder over a screen. The audio is okay, and the video quality is very good in bright and moderate light. In very low light, it starts to suffer as most camcorders in this price range do until it eventually becomes almost unusable.

I am not enamored with the controls. I find that they do not fall where I need them. The still camera is only okay, though it does give a 12 MP image. Get a DSLR or quality P&S if you are serious about still images.

If you want a very good, moderate cost camcorder for moderate to bright lighting and can live with the controls, this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Sony DCR-SX45 Handycam Camcorder (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Electronics UN49KS8000 49-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2016 Model) I was hesitant to buy a TV online but went to several local stores and many were out of stock since they were transitioning to 2017 models. So I decided to try Amazon on this 2016 Samsung that had many good reviews and was a good price. I was very impressed with both the TV and the delivery from Amazon.
Delivery: I was able to select which day I wanted it delivered and then was kept updated on the delivery status by Amazon. The delivery company called a few days in advance to verify a 3 hour window of time, and they did arrive that day within the window of time even though it was 10 min prior to the end of that time. They brought the TV in, removed it from the boxing, placed it on our TV stand, plugged it in and verified it was functioning. They took a picture of the functioning TV and took the old box/trash away. I was very pleased with the delivery.
The TV: It is great! Have only used the TV for four days but it has been used a lot during that timeframe. We replaced an older Samsung flatscreen (HD TV) with this one and wow, what a difference. Out of the box without any tuning whatsoever this is a great looking deep colored screen. With a few tweaks it is amazing. There were easy step-by-step onscreen setup instructions. The remote is lot better than the older large clunky devices and is a smart remote that even recognizes voice commands. I liked the concept of having just one cable to the TV which then links to a hub where you plug in other devices. Only issue I had was the TV remote could not recognize my Tivo device from my cable provider for all functions, but it did change channels and volume. I use a generic remote anyway which worked great with the new TV. The bezel is very small and the thickness of the TV is perfect for us.
Overall I was impressed with this TV and would highly recommend it, especially at the discounted price. I’ve already seen reviews of the 2017 version of this TV and some are not very favorable so I'm glad I bought this one.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Electronics UN49KS8000 49-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2016 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000 Though I have a laptop, I decided to use this solid-state drive as a boot drive on my desktop computer. If you are unfamiliar with the difference between a solid-state and a regular hard drive, the solid-state has no moving parts, which makes it silent, fast, reliable, and shock resistant. It has twice the capacity and twice the speed of the solid-state drive I got a couple of years ago for the same price, and blows away a standard drive for speed.

Given the silence and speed, it makes a great boot drive for running Windows, Photoshop, and other programs where speed is a huge advantage. Just to give you an idea, when upgrading from a regular two-year-old hard drive to this solid-state drive, my Windows boot time went from two minutes to about 10 seconds. Seriously, my computer now starts up and is ready to use in like 10 seconds.

What I do is use a solid-state drive as my boot drive and a regular hard drive as a storage drive. Solid-state drives like this are really expensive to purchase if you need any kind of capacity, but a 200 GB drive will certainly hold all of your programs and often used files.

As for this drive specifically, I hooked it up to my desktop and it was immediately recognized by Windows. The drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up as a drive and work in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

As I said, it's a lot faster than the solid-state drive I had from a couple years ago, and there's no problem using it on my desktop machine rather than my laptop.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000

I used a dB meter that was about 6ft away with the speaker pointed towards the meter. At max volume on my main phone (fold3) and at 150% volume, I was getting a consistent mid-90s dB for melody and lyrics, with peaks up to 109dB. On my other device (Note 10+), also at 150%, it was pulling about 70 dB on TV dialogue. I did try testing it with a volume booster, and even with only 110% (on top of the 150%) it was beginning to distort.
I played the TV audio for about 16hrs at moderate and 8hrs on low, and it was reading as still having 70% battery. But after only a few hours of moderate-high volume music, that 70% was gone and it died.
The sound quality is quite good with a warm tone. The highs are clear and the bass is better than I expected for there not to be a dedicated bass cone.
Despite appearances, I think the best use for this will be background music - not too loud will keep it playing all day & night and it will provide a much cleaner and richer sound than a small speaker at similar volume.

text_fidelity_a:
Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF When I opened the package containing this MP3 player, I was amazed at how small it is. But immediately became delighted at its perfectly small size. It is not the size of a small cellphone, but rather like what should have naturally occurred if an iPod shuffle mated with an iPod Nano. Perfect size and perfect function.

As the product description does not list or show the size of this MP3 player I list them here:

Length: 2 3/4 inches Width: 2 inches Thickness: 3/8 inch

Yes, small, but a powerhouse in functionality. I really miss the days when an MP3 player just played music. After a near fatal fall of my phone (luckily just the screen protector cracked!) it became important that an expensive phone might not be the best thing to lug around while performing yardwork. This excellent device solves that issue, and solves it well.

Songs and MP3 audio books were loaded easily onto the player. It is not made by Apple nor is part of their line, so the iTunes program does not work with this. However, it is a easy fix - just go to your Music folder on your computer, and drop the files you wish into this device's memory. Easy peasy and quick. It comes with an included 32 GB of memory, but can easily be upgraded if you install your own micro SD card, up to 128 GB.

It comes with wired earphones, which I did not use or test. With the invention of easy to pair Bluetooth earphones, I have no desire to be ever tethered with a headphone cord again. The player pairs easily with all 3 of my Bluetooth devices - earphones, headphones, and speakers. The sound from each device is flawless, which might be a function of the device, but is also determined by the source.

There are just 3 buttons on the side of this MP3 player - on/off button, volume up, and volume down. All other functions are controlled by the small but well designed touch screen. It is very comparable with the touch capability of modern phones, the programs are opened with ease and operate in an intuitive logical manner. There are other functions built into this device, but since I really got it as an MP3 player, that is what I am focused upon.

With this player comes a handy removable back clip, letting you clip it on/in a pocket, armband, belt, anywhere. Without the clip, it is small enough to easily slip into any pocked of your cloths, even the tiny change pockets in most jeans. Besides the wired earphones & clip, there is a 3mm audio cable for attaching it manually to another device, and a Micro USB cable for charging. There is a plastic protective film on the front face - it can be removed, but the touch screen operates just fine if it is left on.

This is my new favorite toy, It it not cheap or flimsy, but in all honesty, looks and feels like a tiny cell phone in how its constructed. It does not happen often, but this wonderful MP3 player exceeded my expectations.
text_fidelity_b: FDY MP3 Player, MP3 Player with Bluetooth5.0, 32GB Portable Music Player with FM Radio/Recorder, HiFi Lossless Sound Quality, 2.4Inch Touch Screen Mini MP3 Player for Running, Expandable 128GB TF

This frame was easy to figure out, though, at least for the features I care about. I skipped right over the parts where it wanted to connect to my network and so forth. I just wanted to upload photos from a micro-SD card, and then have it play them back to me. And it does that very well.

It has a light sensor that adjusts the brightness of the screen automatically if you enable it to, which is a very nice feature that is lacking on my other digital picture frames. I was also able to program it to go to sleep when I'm never up, to save on energy. I didn't want it to be motion activated, as I want it to be displaying photos the moment I walk into the room. Fortunately, this feature is already off by default.

The frame looks really nice, with a small "mat" border around the display. This mat is something that most digital frames are lacking, and let me tell you, this tiny feature makes a huge difference. It really sells the idea that this is a picture frame, instead of merely a digital display. I can't say enough about how much this improves the aesthetic of this frame.

I have a couple of digital frames that I use in a horizontal orientation, so I deleted all my vertical photos from them and moved them onto this one instead, and set it up in a vertical orientation. It is so nice to have the frame matched to the orientation of the photos! You don't get those huge bars on the sides or top/bottom, or if you have it set to crop then you don't crop out 2/3 of the photo!

I have no complaints about this digital photo frame. I can't speak for all of the features, because I have no use for some of them. But the features I wanted work great, and the frame itself looks fantastic!
text_fidelity_b: MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame

That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.
text_fidelity_b: SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link Deco Whole Home Mesh WiFi System (Deco S4) – Up to 2,000 Sq.ft. Coverage, WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Gigabit Ports, 1-Pack Been using for a few months now. Initially seemed like an excellent upgrade over an inexpensive single wifi router, but I've seen enough issues that I'm not sure I'd buy again. The worst failure was when I switched from Verizon Fios coax to ethernet and tried to use this as my main router. It worked... for about a week. At first, I just had trouble connecting to corp sites, so I thought it might be my corp network. Later that day, I saw issues with personal devices. Connecting to the router web page was super sluggish and the cpu was pegged. The next day, I went back to using the verizon router as the wired backbone and only using this set for wifi---much better. But, I still see occasional flakiness. Yesterday, one of the units wouldn't connect. I brought it closer to the other units---no dice. I rebooted. I connected it to the network via an ethernet cable. Finally, I rebooted the main/router unit and things went back to normal. Every 2-4 weeks one of the units has issues. Sometimes rebooting that unit is enough. Occasionally I have to reboot the main unit. One of the extender units connects via both wifi and powerline. The other extender unit only connects via powerline (it's too far to use wifi). The powerline-only unit is the one that tends to have issues. But, that was the point of buying this system.

So, the system seems good as long as you don't mind doing a ~weekly reboot. I see about 30Mbps over the powerline-only unit---not fast, but generally reliable.

I've started using MoCA (ethernet over coax) and will likely use that as my backbone in the near future---it's faster (I've seen ~300Mbps for a local transfer over MoCA/ethernet/wifi) and seems to be more reliable than this tp-link set over powerline.

Edit: I ditched this in favor of an EdgeRouter X and Ubiquity access points and am happier now. The Deco system was okay, but far from ideal.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link Deco Whole Home Mesh WiFi System (Deco S4) – Up to 2,000 Sq.ft. Coverage, WiFi Router/Extender Replacement, Gigabit Ports, 1-Pack

text_fidelity_a: NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Ethernet Smart Switch (GS108T) - Managed, with 1 x PD Port, Optional Insight Cloud Management, Desktop or Wall Mount, Silent Operation, and Limited Lifetime Protection This is the first switch that I have owned that can be configured. Once you determine the IP address of the switch, you simply enter it in your browser, enter the default password (which you can change) and you are into the setup program that is internal to the switch.  You can do individual settings for each of the 8 ports, if you know what the settings mean (I didn't.)  This is an optional thing; you can use the switch without any configuration; just plug it in and it is ready to go.  There are two reasons why I didn't give this a 5 star rating.  1) The indicator lights showing active ports are on the same side as the cables.  Since I want cables to go out the back, I can't see the lights with the switch facing me.  My prior switch had lights on one side and cables went out the other.  In all honesty, I can't say that the lights ever provided much benefit and could be distracting, so this might be an advantage to some people to have both lights and cables on the back.  What's the point of the lights if you can't see them, unless you want the cables facing you?  2) In order to register the switch and get a program to determine the IP address of the switch (so that you can configure it), you have to use a mobile device (a smart phone) and install the Netgear Insight application and set up a Netgear account.  Strange that you need to use a device other than a computer to do this and it is rather a nuisance.  Apparently there is no Windows version of Netgear Insight.  You have to use your IOS or Android device.  Another problem I had is that you supposedly can change your password on your device, which I tried, but apparently the password did not meet the requirements, but was never informed of that by the program.  I was able to change the password on the device after getting into it via the IP address.  Netgear makes good products and I have purchased other Netgear products in the past with good results.  This is another quality product, so if the placement of the lights doesn't bother you, I would recommend it, especially if you need individually configurable ports.

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) I use earbuds a lot since I typically prefer the lightness and ease of use compared with traditional headphones. Right out of the box these were a bit puzzling as to how to position them for use. But, after a bit of fiddling with the over-the-ear loop, it becomes clear.

The in-ear comfort is good. It comes with a variety of ear tips including two types I’ve not used before: a double flange silicon tip and a triple flange silicon tip. The flanges allow the ear bud to make a much better seal in your ear canal. That not only helps cut out ambient noise intruding, it also improves the bass response. I found the double flange works best for me, but the variety of tips included appears sufficient to fit pretty much any ear.

It also comes with an excellent case for storage, and adapters for airplane use and for 1/4 inch plugs. I especially like the case since it’s small enough to make it easy to carry along (roughly 3.5 inches by 3 by 1.5 inches thick) and is reinforced to avoid being crushed. It has mesh pockets to keep everything stowed, and looks nice to boot (black with red contrast in the middle). All-in-all, it’s a great kit in terms of useful accessories.

I’m not as pleased with the cord. While I like how sturdy it is, it has a “Y” link that always seems to be in the way when I’m working out. I got used to it eventually, but a more streamlined cord system would have been a better design approach. Another negative is the 3.5mm plug. It needs to be seated just so or you get sound cut-outs or static. I tried it with several devices to be sure the issue is with the plug and not the device. A more robust plug is needed for this – you shouldn’t have to fiddle with it to get it to seat properly.

The over-the-ear loops are also a bit annoying at first. Granted, that’s certainly due to the fact that I usually use standard in-ear buds without the loop, so any type of loop feels weird to me at first. The material is soft and bendy, so you can position it in any variety of ways. It could benefit from some additional padding. On the plus side, they do hold the buds in very well. Quick head movements that would have loosened an in-ear bud didn’t jar these loose at all.

Now for the really important feature: how they sound. In a word, excellent. My benchmark for moderately-priced earbuds has been units made by RHA out of the UK. These sound nearly as good. Very clean sound but still ample bass provided that you select the right tip. For me, the standard tip (the one installed as delivered) gave me very little in terms of bass. Selecting a different tip to provide a better ear fit did wonders for bass response.

They are a bit more airy than the RHA sound. That could be a plus or a minus depending on your preferred type of music. Very heavy bass music is not a good match for these. Pretty much everything else is, and I appreciated the enhanced clarity. It’s the type of sound that, when you hear it, the first word that would come to mind is “clean.”

They look odd, make take you a moment to figure out how to position them, but provide a very open, natural sound. It comes with a well-designed kit of useful extras. However, the plug issues, the cord, and the ear loops collectively knock it down a star. Still well worth considering, however, and I would certainly recommend them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

text_fidelity_a:
Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green) I've been testing this speaker system with my 10" Samsung Galaxy Tab2 tablet which had no problems connecting to the speakers with and without the app from the Android store.

Appearance:
Their product description calls this 'fun, trendy and modern'. But to be honest this looks, to me, like an appliance that fell out of my grandmother's 1950's black, white and chrome art-deco kitchen. It's not unpleasant looking but I wouldn't call it modern. When I saw images of the system online I had hopes that the neon green ring around the face would light up. Sadly it doesn't. The handle is also fixed in place and doesn't retract or collapse into the body. It would have been a nice idea so you could stack or store this more easily.

Sound:
It doesn't sound bad. Especially for being just two 15 watt wide range speakers in a ported (holes to help the bass sound better) enclosure. The bass is a little flat and the high end sounds a little... hollow but it is a lot better than the speakers built into my tablet. I've tried a variety of music; jazz, pop, classical, rock, punk and everything sounded quite good. I found I had to use both the tablet's volume control as well as the speaker systems volume controls to get real volume out of the system. They operate independently of each other.

Drawbacks:
I don't normally comment on price with items received from the Vine program but at the time I'm writing this review Amazon is currently selling this item for over two hundred dollars. Maybe the Bluetooth equipment is expensive but to me that's a LOT for just two speakers in a box. I didn't pay that much for my four speaker bookshelf system or the subwoofer equipped speaker system connected to my desktop PC. Both of which have far superior sound quality.

The battery indicator light only seems to light up when the system is charging. I charged this a week ago and used it for several hours at a time but I have no idea how much charge is left in the battery.

The biggest problem I had with this speaker system was when doing anything other than playing music. I thought it would be fun to add big sound to the games I enjoy on my tablet but there's a distinct lag between doing anything and when the speaker plays the sound. I noticed it most of all in my favorite billiards simulator. You would strike a ball...and then hear it happen, even system sounds such as keyboard typing noises, a 'blip' when selecting things played a noticeable time after they happened.

The App:
I won't say much about the app here. It's completely unnecessary to operate this system with your Android device. It's just poor quality programming that appears to have been slapped together at the last minute. It also doesn't match the documentation and features such as Bass Boost which are in the instructions but don't exist in the app.

Speaking of the documentation. I opened the box and found a large booklet and for one, brief, moment I thought this item was fully documented in depth and detail... then I opened the instructions and found there's twelve pages of English instructions which are poorly written and lacking in detail. The rest of the book is comprised of numerous other languages each getting their own few pages. Ah well. Turn it on, turn it up. Enjoy the music.
text_fidelity_b: Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green)

Occasionally it would just drop from the internet at random and then I could easily connect it. Most of the time, however, it would work great! We use it for a light since most of our house works on light switches that are not conveniently placed near the doors, so we trip around at night over stuff to get to the actual lights to turn them on without the smart plugs. Well after a storm and a power surge this past week, the plug in our bedroom showed as disconnected in the app. I have tried multiple times over multiple days to reconnect it. I contacted Amazon via chat to fix the issue (after troubleshooting myself) and they only suggested resetting the plug (which I had already done) and restarting our entire home system and each Amazon Smart Device (which we did after the power surge due to other devices not working). After an hour and a half, they basically said well its out of warranty so you need to buy a new one. They did offer a discount but the discount was to be issued as a refund after purchase and the amount to be paid was significantly more then what I originally paid. We have 2 other smart plugs of a different brand that are as old as this plug that have had absolutely no issues to date and cost about $5 each when we purchased them as well. Not to mention the Amazon Smart Plug is bulky and takes up so much more space then the smaller round off-brand ones. Due to the fact that this plug didn't last a long time and the actual price is so high to begin with I would not recommend this plug. Spend the money on an off-brand!

I have $400 Sennheisers and after listening to these for a while I had to swap out to see what the sound difference was. And I definitely cannot say that these are just as good, but I cannot say that the difference would justify an additional $300+. Especially when I was looking for a pair for my kids to use on road trips.

The kids did appreciate them. They are not completely isolating but they isolated enough to let them listen to their music over road noise while driving. They will definitely be a part of our road trip equipment from now on.

The fit seems to be better for the kids than for me. Perhaps my head is too big, but they felt a bit tight for me. Kids report they fit great. I'm not sure that an audiophile would really appreciate these, but for the price, my kids love them.

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This bag arrived just before we went out of town for a trip, and the timing couldn’t have been better. My wife has a 13” laptop that she loves and uses daily, and this bag was the perfect solution for carrying it on the trip. It isn’t necessarily the most fancy bag but it gets the job done and it seems to be made well. I would make one alteration to make it better, based on experiences I have had with similar bags in the past.

This is a smaller bag, not designed to hold 15.6” or larger laptops, so it is not going to help people who have “standard” laptop sizes unless this is going to be used as a book bag instead. If you need a bag that fits a laptop that is 15.6” or greater, this one will not work for you. That’s okay as it is very clearly marketed as such so it should come as no surprise. Being for smaller computers doesn’t make it useless though; it does work very well as a book bag and an organizer, so even if you need a larger one for your computer this one has its uses.

This is a leather messenger bag. The leather is a style I have heard referred to as “ruined leather” though that’s not an indicator of the quality. On the contrary, this bag is well made and I can’t find anything about it to suggest that it is made with less care and quality than the price dictates. In spite of the appearance, the materials are quality and I cannot find any blemishes or cuts, the stitching is straight and all the clasps and zippers work properly.

There are plenty of pockets to store your items and keep organized. Of course there this the main compartment which is designed to hold a computer, but there is room for books as well in the main compartment. There are zippered compartments inside the bag as well as outside, and these are good for carrying your mouse, pens and pencils, passport, maps and other important items.

The flap that covers the main compartment secures to the rest of the bag with straps that fasten with a pressure snap behind a fake decorative buckle, and this represents the one thing about this bag I do not like. If you are not careful and you catch one of the straps on something will walking, you can break the snap and damage or ruin the bag. I have had this happen with other bags using this kind of fastener. I would rather see a magnet used instead which will let go when pulled, or get rid of the decorative buckle and replace it with a real buckle which will hold regardless.

I like this bag. It is well made and it should last for years with proper care. It has room for your smaller laptop as well as books and other supplies. I don’t like the way the flap secures, mainly because if problems I have had with similar bags using similar fasteners, but for the majority of users this is a good solution that is worth consideration. It’s a little more expensive than a canvas bag, but it should last longer.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch
